related_questions.question: What are 5 examples of environmental health?

text_blocks.snippet: Environmental health encompasses various factors that affect human health through our surroundings. Five examples include: clean air, safe water, adequate sanitation, healthy food, and non-toxic environments. These elements are crucial for preventing disease and promoting well-being.
snippet_highlighted_words: clean air, safe water, adequate sanitation, healthy food, and non-toxic environments

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a more detailed look at each:

list.title: 1. Clean Air:
list.snippet: Access to breathable air, free from pollutants like particulate matter and harmful gases, is essential for respiratory health and overall well-being. Poor air quality can lead to respiratory illnesses, cardiovascular problems, and even cancer, according to Verywell Health.

list.title: 2. Safe Water:
list.snippet: Ensuring access to clean and safe drinking water is vital for preventing waterborne diseases and maintaining hydration, according to Verywell Health. Contaminated water can cause illnesses like cholera, dysentery, and typhoid.

list.title: 3. Adequate Sanitation:
list.snippet: Proper sanitation, including access to functioning toilets and waste disposal systems, is crucial for preventing the spread of diseases and maintaining hygiene. Poor sanitation can lead to outbreaks of infectious diseases and contribute to environmental contamination.

list.title: 4. Healthy Food:
list.snippet: Access to nutritious and safe food is fundamental for physical and mental development, as well as overall health. Poor food safety practices can lead to foodborne illnesses, while inadequate access to healthy food can result in malnutrition.

list.title: 5. Non-Toxic Environments:
list.snippet: Living and working in environments free from harmful chemicals and pollutants is vital for preventing a range of health issues. This includes exposure to heavy metals, pesticides, and other toxins found in air, water, soil, and consumer products.
